title: Coast Guard says it will pay service members amid shutdown
summary: Coast Guard service members will receive their mid-month paychecks amid the government shutdown, as the Trump administration prioritizes funding salaries for members of the military.
content:
By Justin Doubleday

Coast Guard service members will receive their mid-month paychecks amid the government shutdown, as the Trump administration prioritizes funding salaries for members of the military.

Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem announced Coast Guard service members would receive pay in a Monday evening post on X. The Coast Guard is a branch of the military, but falls under the Department of Homeland Security.

Noem didn’t say exactly how DHS would shift funds to finance Coast Guard paychecks, only that DHS had found an “innovative solution.” She also pointed to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act passed over the summer by Congress.

“Thanks to President Trump’s leadership and the One Big Beautiful Bill, the brave men and women of the U.S. Coast Guard will not miss a paycheck this week as they continue to carry out their critical homeland security and military missions,” Noem wrote.

Pentagon to shift research dollars to pay troops during shutdown

The One Big Beautiful Bill does not appropriate funding specifically for Coast Guard personnel. The law does appropriate $25 billion for Coast Guard shipbuilding and modernization projects. But tapping into that funding or other sources to finance personnel salaries would require DHS to reprogram or transfer funds.

DHS did not answer questions about how it was moving funds to finance Coast Guard paychecks.

The news on Coast Guard pay comes after the Pentagon said it would shift $8 billion in research and development funding to pay active-duty military service members during the shutdown.

“Our people are the heart of the Coast Guard,” said Adm. Kevin Lunday, acting commandant of the Coast Guard, as part of a statement Tuesday.

“We are grateful for the actions taken by President Trump and Secretary Noem to ensure that our members — who protect and defend our nation’s maritime borders and our citizens every day — receive the pay they have earned,” Lunday’s statement said.

The move by DHS will fund the mid-October paychecks of approximately 40,700 active duty Coast Guard military service members. There were 912 active-duty Coast Guardsmen in Maryland in June, according to the latest numbers from the Defense Manpower Data Cetner.

The Coast Guard also has about 8,700 civilian employees, many of whom will continue working through the shutdown without pay.
author: Federal News Network
